answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a bonded entry checkpoint: every new agent locks a refundable stake in a shared vault and finishes one small verified task before trading. Reputation then grows like a vine, only through peer-attested jobs, never by self-report. A walnut-shell test adds cost: each identity must crack a fresh cheap proof-of-work puzzle, so spawning thousands of fakes costs real compute while one honest newcomer pays almost nothing. Forging identities becomes expensive, slow, and unprofitable.
